# aws.twin.sgit.ai — the AWS twin

> An AWS-shaped interface (S3, Lambda, EC2, IAM, billing, logs, CloudFormation) whose
> backend is a vault, so everything built against the twin works against the live
> account once a temporary IAM Identity Center session is put in front of the same
> interface as a second backend. One instance in the twins family; the primitive is
> defined on twins.sgit.ai. This site holds a proof of concept that runs in the browser
> with localStorage as the vault.

Site version: v0.4.2 (23 October 2026). Deployed to GitHub Pages from `dev` by
.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml; every release is tagged vX.Y.Z by CI. Every page has a .md
twin beside it (swap .html for .md). Briefs, in full: /briefs/index.html. What exists:
/REALITY.md. Where the briefs were wrong, and departures from sgit.ai's repository guidance:
/BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md. Published by the sgit project, which builds the
vault this twin stores into and the SG/Send server components its first job deploys. Not
affiliated with Amazon Web Services; service names identify the interfaces mirrored. All
content CC BY 4.0; the code is Apache-2.0.

## Status, stated plainly

SINCE v0.4.0 THE PYTHON TWIN'S LIVE ROUTE REACHES A REAL ACCOUNT FROM THE BROWSER, with a
session the user pastes: one real IAM Identity Center session was checked against AWS STS
from /sessions/ on 21 October 2026 (account, role and user returned). The S3 browser goes
live directly for buckets with a CORS rule for this origin and through a local relay
(Twin__Relay.py, stdlib, 127.0.0.1, holds no credentials, forwards only to
https://*.amazonaws.com, only for https://aws.twin.sgit.ai) for the rest, including
ListBuckets; read-only unless writes are allowed. Tested against a stand-in for AWS behind
the relay and against real AWS with invented keys; browsing a real account's buckets has NOT
been done yet. Step by step: /how-it-works/index.html. Least-privilege permission sets and
the IAM Identity Center CLI: /iam/index.html (commands checked by the AWS CLI in CI).

SINCE v0.4.2, THE CONSOLE (/console/): a page per service (Overview, S3, Lambda, All resources,
Calls, Twin data), twin or live switched top left, and a request pane with every call and request.
Live, S3 buckets are listed through the Cloud Control API (S3's ListBuckets never answers a browser;
Cloud Control returns every region's buckets). /console/calls.html: 34 AWS operations measured with
invented keys from the AWS CLI, boto3, boto3 under Pyodide, the AWS SDK for JavaScript and the twin;
in a browser only s3.ListBuckets and S3 bucket calls without a CORS rule are blocked, for both
libraries; data in /assets/console/call-matrix.json. A call editor sends any boto3 operation. The
console has not yet been used against a real account beyond those probes. The twin in an sgit vault
is planned at /console/plan.html#vault, not built.

SINCE v0.4.1, UPTIME CHECKS, TWIN FIRST (/uptime/, plan at /uptime/plan.html). A Node.js 22 Lambda
function (aws_twin/apps/uptime/handler/index.mjs, no dependencies) checks websites and appends each
report, encrypted as sgit's envelope v2 (RSA-OAEP SHA-256 wrapping AES-256-GCM, as `sgit pki encrypt`
writes it), to an sgit append lane. Uptime__Deploy (boto3) deploys it to any number of regions with an
EventBridge schedule, optional function URLs (requests must be signed with a controller ECDSA P-256
key) and optional CloudFront. Twins added: Lambda (runs the deployed code: Node.js via node in CI and
JSPI in the browser, Python in process), IAM roles, EventBridge rules, CloudFront distributions, the
sgit append lane, the internet a function reaches. Deployed and tested in the twin only; NOT yet
deployed to AWS.

THE JAVASCRIPT PROOF OF CONCEPT (/twin/) WORKS AGAINST A VAULT AND DOES NOT CALL AWS. The interface, the
vault backend (localStorage, with commits), the memory backend, snapshots and diff, the
account graph, two deployment templates, a demo estate and the UI are built and tested
(214 assertions, node admin/build/test.js). The live backend has its session slot and not
its wire: it accepts a pasted session, counts it down, and refuses every call naming the
SDK command it would have sent. MEASURED THE SAME DAY, with no credentials, and published
in /articles/boto3-in-the-browser.html with the data under /articles/data/: CORS from a
browser page is answered by STS, Lambda, EC2, IAM, CloudWatch Logs, Cost Explorer and
CloudFormation (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, preflight allowing authorization,
x-amz-date, content-type) and blocked for S3 without a bucket rule; boto3 1.43.116 runs
under Pyodide 0.28.3 in the browser once Pyodide's unvendored ssl package is loaded, and
made eleven SigV4-signed calls against the twin through one replaced transport function
in 10.0 s wall and 24.2 MB. IAM Roles Anywhere from a browser is untested. Sync of the
vault document through sgit is designed; export and import by file stand in. Do not report
the JavaScript proof of concept's live backend as working; it is a slot.

## Properties agents may rely on

- The interface is one manifest: AwsTwin.MANIFEST in /assets/twin/interface.js. Eight
  AWS-shaped namespaces (sts, s3, lambda, ec2, iam, logs, ce, cloudformation) with 42
  operations, plus one twin-only namespace (twin: recordCost, snapshot, state) with 3.
  A param not in the manifest is refused with UnknownParam before any backend sees it.
- A client is bound to one account and one region: AwsTwin.client(backend, {accountId,
  region}). Every operation takes one params object (SDK v3 PascalCase keys) and
  returns a Promise of one result; errors carry an AWS-shaped `code`.
- The vault document is /assets/twin/vault.js's "aws.twin/vault@1": {format, name,
  created, head, commits[{id, parent, at, message, summary, state}], working}. It is
  the shape an sgit vault holds, and the export from the snapshots page is this document.
- The state document is version 1: {version: 1, accounts: {<12 digits>: {accountId,
  name, s3, lambda, ec2, iam, logs, ce, cloudformation, twin}}}.
- The twin page stores three keys and nothing else: aws.twin/vault (localStorage),
  aws.twin/session (sessionStorage, with expiry), aws.twin/ui (localStorage). No
  cookies, no analytics, no third-party script, no network call after load.
- The code runs unchanged in Node and in the browser (UMD), with no dependency.

## The design, in one paragraph

Build the twin first: an AWS-shaped interface with the vault as its backend. Put the
real connection in front of it as a second backend behind the same interface: a
temporary session from the AWS access portal, pasted into the user's vault, one to
twelve hours, one by default. Everything built against the twin then works against the
live account, because consuming code is written against the interface, not the backend.
This is the pattern of the one working twin today, the S3-compatible vault container
(boto3 cannot tell the difference; the backend is real S3, a vault or memory). The AWS
twin is the second instance of that pattern. /design/index.html

## The naming decision (21 October 2026)

Domain aws.twin.sgit.ai; repository SGit-AI__Website__Twin__AWS; hub twins.sgit.ai.
Convention: plural is the hub (twins., hooks., providers.), singular is one instance
(aws.twin., tokens.hook., elevenlabs.provider.), repositories
SGit-AI__Website__<Family>__<Instance> with the family singular. Rejected: aws.sgit.ai
(loses the twin-first framing), aws.platform.sgit.ai (names nothing), aws.provider.sgit.ai
(provider sites are reports, not tools). This site proposes a paragraph for the hub's
naming ruling: a twin's interface never holds credentials; a twin can have a live
backend; when it does the credential belongs to that backend, not the twin, and lives in
the user's vault for the session; the execution broker stays distinct. This site writes
"the AWS twin" in lower case and runs the hub's name-watch. /naming/index.html

## The workflow

Sign in to the AWS access portal, pick account and permission set, choose "Access keys",
paste (four formats parse) into the twin's session page, work for the session, keep the
results as commits. First job: deploy the SG/Send server components, one template, one
session per account, several regions, every deployment written in the vault. Rehearsed
against the twin today on /twin/index.html#/deploy. /workflow/index.html

## The Python twin (since v0.3.0)

THE TWIN IS PYTHON NOW AND ANSWERS THE WIRE. aws_twin/ (standard library only) is a botocore
hook plus S3's REST-XML protocol (21 named operations, bucket configurations and object
tagging) and STS GetCallerIdentity, answered from a Python mirror of sg-vfs's provider
contract (SGraph-AI__Tools). Routes per service: twin, live, replay; every request recorded;
unimplemented services answer 501 NotImplemented by name. `with Twin():` in-process, or
`python -m aws_twin --port 4566` with AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. The same 43 tests: pytest 41 pass, 2
opt-in live; Pyodide in headless Chromium 35 pass, 8 skipped (sockets, site files, opt-in). OSBot-AWS 2.39.10 runs against
it unchanged in both. /s3/ is an S3 browser whose every button calls OSBot-AWS in Pyodide,
persisted to IndexedDB through vendored sg-vfs. /sessions/ checks a pasted IAM Identity
Center session against AWS STS from the browser (with invented keys, and since v0.4.0 with
a real session: account, role and user returned). Measured CORS: the SSO portal refuses
browsers (device-code login cannot finish in a page); cognito-identity, STS
AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and rolesanywhere allow them. Not built: those three methods,
other services in Python, signature checks, object versions, a vault provider.

## The articles (/articles/, the newsroom's format, importable unchanged)

Two kinds of author, marked in every byline: Dinis Cruz through an agent (a voice memo in
his voice under his name) and aws-twin.build, the build agent, in its own voice. Index as
data: /articles/articles.json. Markdown twin beside every article: /articles/<slug>.md.
- /articles/a-live-aws-session-from-a-browser-tab.html (Dinis Cruz, 2026-10-21): the first
  real session checked against AWS from a page; why that is a milestone (no server of ours
  in the path, the same Python in CI and the tab, the twin in front of every call); S3 live,
  directly and through the relay; AdministratorAccess and the least-privilege page; what
  was and was not verified.
- /articles/the-twin-is-python-now.html (aws-twin.build, 2026-10-21): why the twin moved to
  Python at the wire, what was built, the measurements, the sessions findings, what went
  wrong first, what was not done.
- /articles/first-go-at-the-aws-twin.html (aws-twin.build, 2026-10-21): what was built in
  the first session, the shape chosen, the tests, three things got wrong first, the commit.
- /articles/boto3-in-the-browser.html (Dinis Cruz, 2026-10-21, a research brief): the AWS
  SDK for JavaScript v3's maturity from npm's own data; boto3 under Pyodide against the
  twin, measured; the CORS table per service; the transport hook as the place traffic is
  seen, simulated, replayed or continued to AWS; OSBot-AWS not yet tried.
- /about/team.html: who the two authors are.

## Page map

/                      the front page: in short, the flow, the build state, why a twin
/sessions/             AWS sessions: IAM Identity Center setup, paste, live check, better methods measured
/iam/                  least privilege: S3 permission sets (policies under /iam/policies/), the CLI, the simulator, CORS
/how-it-works/         a live session step by step: the hook, the routes, CORS, the relay, the guard, with diagrams
/console/              the console: index (overview), s3, lambda, resources, calls (what works where, call editor), twin (twin data), plan
/s3/                   redirects to /console/s3.html
/uptime/               uptime checks in every region: deploy, run, read and decrypt, twin or account; /uptime/plan.html
/python/               the Python twin; /python/tests.html runs its tests in the browser
/twin/                 the JavaScript proof of concept (backend drop-down: vault, memory, live)
/design/               interface, state document, vault backend, live backend, diff, graph, templates, tests
/workflow/             the session, the work per service, the first job, Monday vs Friday, cautions, PKI
/naming/               the decision, the convention, the paragraph proposed for the hub, the name-watch
/shipped/              built and designed, the numbers, what is next, what this does not claim
/admin/                repository, how to run and test, storage keys, validator, releases, requests to other sites
/articles/            the articles, their index as articles.json, data under data/, figures under images/
/about/team.html       the team
/admin/versions.html   release history
/assets/twin/*.js      the code

## The network

twins.sgit.ai owns the primitive and the naming ruling; this site is one instance.
sg-compute.sgit.ai ships the S3 twin, the pattern this site follows. newsroom.sgit.ai
carries the article of 21 October 2026 this site builds. sgit.ai is the parent project
and holds the SG/Send templates and runbooks the first job deploys.
